test_title: PYST 3: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Why has ISRO proposed the development of a third launch pad beyond the existing facilities at Sriharikota?

options.text: To serve exclusively as a data relay hub for enhancing satellite telemetry
To accommodate space tourism missions under future commercial programmes
To provide backup support in case of emergency ground failures during launches
To handle increasing launch frequency and capacity for missions involving SSLV, Gaganyaan, and commercial payloads

solution:
The correct answer is __**To handle increasing launch frequency and capacity for missions involving SSLV, Gaganyaan, and commercial payloads**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** has proposed the development of a third launch pad to address the **increasing demand for satellite launches** and ensure operational efficiency.
 
• The existing launch pads at **Sriharikota** are primarily used for missions involving the PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) and GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) series.
 
• The third launch pad will cater to **Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV)** missions, which are designed for launching smaller satellites into orbit, as well as the upcoming **Gaganyaan** (India's human spaceflight mission).
 
• With the **expansion of commercial payload launches** under the "New Space India Limited (NSIL)" initiative, a new launch pad is critical to meeting global demand and generating revenue for ISRO.
 
• The third pad will also support **higher launch frequency**, ensuring a faster turnaround time between missions to accommodate both government and commercial clients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV):**

 
 
• The SSLV is a smaller, cost-effective launcher developed by ISRO for deploying small satellites into low Earth orbit.
 
• It is designed to cater to the growing demand for small satellite launches, including nano and microsatellites.
 
• The SSLV is considered a key asset for commercial clients seeking affordable and quick satellite deployment.
 
 
 
• **Gaganyaan Mission:**
 
 
• The Gaganyaan is India’s first human spaceflight mission, aiming to carry Indian astronauts (Vyomanauts) into space by 2024.
 
• The third launch pad will play a crucial role in supporting this mission, providing the necessary infrastructure for human-rated launches.
 
 
 
• **New Space India Limited (NSIL):**
 
 
• NSIL is a government-owned company established in 2019 to promote and commercialize ISRO’s technologies and satellite launch services.
 
• The third launch pad will help NSIL expand its commercial offerings and attract international clients.
 
 
 
• **Sriharikota Spaceport:**
 
 
• Located in Andhra Pradesh, Sriharikota is home to the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), the primary launch site for ISRO’s missions.
 
• The first two launch pads at Sriharikota have been operational for decades, supporting landmark missions like Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ISRO’s Global Standing:**

 
 
• ISRO has emerged as a reliable and cost-effective partner for satellite launches, with a strong global reputation for precision and affordability.
 
• The third launch pad will further bolster India’s position in the international space market by increasing launch capacity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Benefits:**
 
 
• The increase in launch frequency and capacity will drive significant revenue generation through commercial satellite launches.
 
• It will also contribute to India’s growing space economy, which is expected to be worth billions in the coming decades.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• The third launch pad will incorporate state-of-the-art technology to support a wide range of missions, from small satellite launches to human spaceflight.
 
• This infrastructure will also play a role in future deep-space missions and interplanetary exploration.
